$comment: The work spigot's dial (#3960). One `work-mode:<position>` label on trackingIssue sets how fast every autonomous lane pulls work; scripts/moneypenny/work-mode.mjs reads it and hands lanes the numbers below. Same doctrine as research-circuit-breaker.json: the STATE is an issue label (never a committed file, #915), this file only holds the per-position numbers, and a missing or malformed file refuses to run rather than defaulting to unlimited.
$why: Eric's three scenarios on #3960 (2026-09-28): throttle hard to protect the weekly quota (conserve), shut everything off (halt), and fan out when quota would otherwise be lost at the reset (surge). The phrase-triggered conserve-mode in docs/COMPUTE.md reached only the session that heard it; a label on one issue reaches every lane with one `gh issue view`. Numbers: normal.inFlightCap 3 matches the board's In Progress WIP limit Eric set on 2026-09-30, so the board and the lanes never disagree; normal.researchPerTick 6 matches research-dispatch-budget.json maxPerTick (today's behavior, unchanged). surge doubles normal as a first guess, to be re-sized once the ::notice::cost data for a 6-session tick is measured (#3960 open question). halt is zero everywhere by definition — a brake is a brake. normal.governorDispatches 4 is today's behavior too: `/governor` walks all four athletes in the roster at WIP 1 each, so 4 is one full cycle; conserve 1 is the plan's 'one coach per cycle'; surge 8 lets a coach be dispatched more than once in a cycle, which is the only way a governor cycle goes faster (added #3960 slice 2). grindWidth is the items one `/grind` run may fan out over: normal 200 is grind.js's own MAX_ITEMS sanity cap, so normal changes nothing and surge cannot exceed it without raising that constant; conserve 5 is the plan's 'cap /grind width' made a number — a wider batch is refused with the position named, never silently truncated (added #3960 slice 4).
